analysis.title: Spot Is Four Times The Hurdle: What $50 Billion-A-Gigawatt Neocloud Rents Say About The AI Revenue Gap
key_insights: Goldman's SpaceX Q3 preview (Eric Sheridan) shows AI compute rents of $40-50B per GW per year on short-term deals, $20-30B per GW on long-term hosting, and about $12B per GW as the return hurdle for a hyperscaler.

SpaceX says its hosting deals are monetized at the high end of the ~$30-50bn/GW range. Nebius disclosed Q3 short-term deals at ~$40-50bn/GW, CoreWeave disclosed similar, and long-term deals are pointing to ~$20bn/GW as a pricing floor. IREN disclosed recent 3-year contracts above $25bn/GW.

Deutsche Bank's Edison Yu backs out GPU-hour pricing of SpaceX deals at $50-51M per MW for Google and Reflection AI and $60-61M per MW for two undisclosed customers, as much as $61B per GW, or nearly $14 an hour for GB300s.
The term structure of AI compute is steeply inverted: buyers pay roughly double for not committing. The article reads this as backwardation, meaning the shortage is priced as temporary.
Goldman puts all-in hyperscaler capex at roughly $42B per GW. At $40-50B a year of rent a neocloud recoups the build in about one year, and at the $20B long-term floor in two.
Most SpaceX hosting deals are 90-day cancellable on both sides. Goldman flags that its assumption of revenue at current rates through contract expiry (2029 in most cases) may be overly bullish.
Goldman models SpaceX hosting/IaaS revenue rising from $1B in 2Q26 to over $10B a quarter by 4Q26 and $45.5B in 2027 on about 1GW of capacity, an implied $35-57B per GW.

Goldman's hyperscaler work says the six big US hyperscalers need about $1.42T of cumulative AI revenue in 2028-30, or about $11.6B per GW per year, to earn a 15% ROIC on 2026-27 AI compute spend. Even at 30% ROIC and the highest capex case the figure is at most $18.6B per GW, so short-term neocloud rents are 2-4x that.

Goldman models Google's SpaceX deal at $45B per GW. The article argues the roughly 4x premium reflects power and shell scarcity, not healthy demand. Once self-built capacity catches up, the premium on rented capacity and a large part of neocloud revenue go away.

JPMorgan's Gokul Hariharan says frontier-model vendors earn 60-80% inference gross margins and could earn $20-40B of annual revenue per GW from tokens (vs $10B in 2025). By the article's math, a lab renting a GW at $45B a year would need $110-225B of tokens, three to eleven times JPM's optimistic range, so spot rentals are mostly for training funded by equity or debt.

Rothschild Redburn's Alexander Haissl put Sell ratings on CoreWeave and Nebius last month. His view: top-paying customers are mostly VC-funded startups and big tech using compute for training rather than inference, and training demand lasts only while external capital is available.
Goldman's TMT desk flags Oracle and Broadcom credit spreads as the key indicator of concern over debt-funded AI capex. Oracle 5Y CDS closed at a record 261bp on Thursday.

In Goldman's SpaceX model the ~1GW rented to third parties earns $40.5B per GW, while SpaceX's own AI revenue (Grok, X, enterprise, Cursor) is modeled at $12-13B per GW. Backing hosting deals out of Visible Alpha consensus implies about $8B per GW in 2027 and about $13B in 2028.

Goldman's bull case: if SpaceX monetizes 75% of non-hosting compute at the $20B long-term floor, AI revenue would be about 31% above Street for 2027 and 9% above for 2028. If the 90-day leases are cancelled, SpaceX needs about $18B per GW on reallocated compute in 2028 to hit consensus, which Goldman calls reasonable.
Goldman sees SpaceX capacity growing from 1.4GW in 2Q26 to about 7GW by end-2027 and about 10.6GW by end-2028.
Neocloud, hyperscaler and AI industry revenue largely count the same end-user dollar several times (enterprise to Anthropic, to cloud partner, to SpaceX/CoreWeave, to Nvidia).

The FT reported OpenAI annualized revenue of about $50B at end-September, against a ~$70B figure circulating after investors grossed up OpenAI to match Anthropic's gross reporting. Goldman's Sean Johnstone attributes the gap to gross vs net reporting. Bloomberg said the $50B was itself a projection based on a shorter period.

Brad Gerstner's framework: the top three labs were at a combined ~$100B run-rate in July and need $180-200B by year-end to keep the AI trade intact. That framework mixes gross and net reporting, and part of lab revenue is itself compute revenue.
Apollo data cited: the top 10% of AI customers account for 99.5% of model-serving spend and 99% of neocloud spend.

The article's scaling math: $1.42T at $11.6B per GW implies about 41GW being built by the six hyperscalers. Priced at the 15% ROIC hurdle that is ~$470B a year of AI revenue, at the $20B long-term floor ~$810B, and at ~$45B short-term rates ~$1.8T. Goldman's Portfolio Strategy says the market needs evidence of ~$300B annual AI revenue.
Goldman's Sheridan remains a buyer of SpaceX with a $230 price target, arguing supply constraints give confidence SpaceX can monetize compute at high ROICs even if the deals are canceled.

The article concludes the scarcity premium is the item least likely to survive as capacity multiplies, which would compress neocloud revenue that supports hosting deals, chip-backed SPVs and lab run-rates. It flags the credit market, where chip-collateralized obligations are priced as if spot were forever, as the likely place the gap shows up.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman's Sheridan sees supply constraints and lack of capacity pushing spot rates up, giving confidence SpaceX can monetize compute at high ROICs even if the 90-day hosting deals are canceled.
Rothschild Redburn's Haissl put a Sell on CoreWeave last month, arguing top-paying customers are VC-funded and training demand depends on external capital.
Rothschild Redburn's Haissl put a Sell on Nebius last month on the same view that compute demand from training depends on external capital.

sector_views.rationale: The article argues short-term neocloud rents of $40-50B per GW are a scarcity premium on 90-day paper that is least likely to survive as capacity grows. Goldman's TMT desk says future returns should come from selective winners rather than anything linked to AI capex.

earnings_insights: Goldman models SpaceX hosting/IaaS revenue (estimate) at $1B in 2Q26, over $10B a quarter by 4Q26 and $45.5B in 2027.
Goldman's bull case (estimate) puts SpaceX AI revenue about 31% above Visible Alpha consensus for 2027 and about 9% above for 2028 if 75% of non-hosting compute earns $20B per GW.
Visible Alpha consensus (estimate) implies SpaceX's own compute is monetized at about $8B per GW in 2027 and about $13B in 2028 after backing out hosting deals.
Nebius and IREN disclosed pricing in August (reported): Nebius short-term deals ~$40-50bn/GW and long-term ~$20-25bn/GW, IREN 3-year contracts above $25bn/GW.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A record, flagged by Goldman's TMT desk as the key indicator of concern over debt-funded AI capex.
Reported by the FT. A ~$70B figure circulates on a grossed-up basis, and Bloomberg said the $50B is a projection from a shorter period.

risk_factors: Most SpaceX hosting deals are 90-day cancellable by both sides, so the revenue stream is effectively a quarterly lease.
Scarcity premium compresses as capacity grows: Goldman sees SpaceX going from 1.4GW in 2Q26 to ~7GW by end-2027 and ~10.6GW by end-2028.
Self-built hyperscaler capacity catching up would remove the premium paid for rented capacity.
Customer concentration: neocloud demand rests on a few cash-burning labs and capacity-starved hyperscalers.
Training demand depends on continued availability of external capital (VC, equity, debt).
Inconsistent gross vs net revenue reporting between Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX distorts lab run-rate figures.
Chip-collateralized debt and SPVs are priced as if spot rates persist.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman's TMT desk flags Oracle and Broadcom credit spreads as the key indicator of concern over debt-funded AI capex, with Oracle 5Y CDS at a record 261bp.
Apollo data cited: the top 10% of AI customers make up 99.5% of model-serving spend and 99% of neocloud spend.
geopolitical: The article notes China has a separate and much cheaper AI ecosystem.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Sheridan argues supply constraints keep upward pressure on spot rates, so SpaceX can monetize compute at high ROICs even if the 90-day deals are canceled. Goldman's bull case has AI revenue ~31% above Street for 2027 if 75% of non-hosting compute earns $20B per GW.
tension_points.bear_case: Spot rents of $40-50B per GW are 2-4x the hyperscaler hurdle of about $12B, sit on 90-day cancellable contracts, and are paid mostly for training by capital-funded buyers. The Street models $8-13B per GW for SpaceX's own compute.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Self-built hyperscaler capacity catching up with demand, which ends the scarcity premium.

theme_stances.key_argument: Short-term neocloud rents are a scarcity premium for training on 90-day paper that compresses as capacity multiplies.
theme_stances.evidence: the scarcity premium is the thing least likely to survive

theme_stances.key_argument: Hyperscaler capex needs about $470B to $1.8T a year of AI revenue across the 41GW being built, against about $100B of top-three lab run-rate in July.
theme_stances.evidence: today's neocloud rates are a marginal price for scarce capacity
